title: 📚 What is Lexical Resource?

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: Lexical Resource is one of four equally-weighted criteria in IELTS Writing and Speaking (25% each). It measures not just WHAT words you know, but HOW flexibly and accurately you use them.

sections.heading: The band difference
sections.body:
Band 6 uses common words correctly but repetitively.
Band 7 uses some less common vocabulary with occasional errors.
Band 8 uses a wide range with only minor inaccuracies.
Band 9 uses vocabulary with full flexibility and precise meaning.

highlight: The examiner is NOT counting rare words. They're looking for natural, confident use of a wide range.

example.wrong: The problem is very bad. It is a bad problem that causes bad things.
example.right: The issue is increasingly severe, exacerbating existing social inequalities and undermining long-term economic stability.

meaning: to reduce the severity or seriousness of something
example: Governments must take action to mitigate the effects of climate change.

title: 💡 Remember: mitigate vs exacerbate
body:
These two are often confused and frequently appear in IELTS.

✅ mitigate = make LESS severe → "reduce, lessen, ease"
❌ exacerbate = make MORE severe → "worsen, aggravate, intensify"

They are antonyms — opposite meanings.

question: Which sentence uses "mitigate" correctly?
options: The new law will mitigate the crime rate significantly.
The drought mitigated the water shortage.
Urban trees can mitigate the effects of air pollution.
correct: Urban trees can mitigate the effects of air pollution.
explanation:
✅ Trees REDUCE air pollution — that fits "mitigate" perfectly.

❌ "The new law will mitigate the crime rate" — you mitigate effects/impacts, not rates directly. Better: "reduce the crime rate"
❌ "The drought mitigated the water shortage" — a drought CAUSES a shortage, not reduces it
❌ "Stress can mitigate health problems" — stress WORSENS health; use "exacerbate"
hint: Mitigate always makes something LESS bad, not more bad.

meaning: to make a problem or bad situation worse
example: Poor housing conditions can exacerbate mental health issues.

sentence: Social media can _______ feelings of loneliness among teenagers.
explanation:
Social media makes loneliness WORSE for many teenagers — "exacerbate" is the only word that means "worsen".

"Mitigate" and "alleviate" both mean to reduce/lessen. "Reduce" is too simple for Band 7+.
hint: Social media makes loneliness better or worse?

example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society.
wrong: very rare or hard to find

instruction: Arrange the words to make a correct sentence:
correct: Technology has become ubiquitous in the modern workplace.
explanation:
The correct structure is: Subject (Technology) + auxiliary (has) + verb (become) + adjective (ubiquitous) + prepositional phrase (in the modern workplace).

Note the article "the" before "modern workplace" — we say "the modern workplace" as a concept.

meaning: to increase rapidly in numbers or amount
example: Fast food chains have proliferated across developing nations.
family: proliferation (n) — "the proliferation of social media platforms"

instruction: Match each word to its correct meaning:
explanation: These four words form a powerful vocabulary cluster. Knowing them all helps you discuss problems and changes at Band 8 level.

meaning: to provide evidence to support or prove something
example: The researcher substantiated her claims with longitudinal data.

title: ✏️ Spot the Vocabulary Error
instruction: One sentence uses a word incorrectly. Which one?

sentences.text: The study substantiated the link between diet and longevity.
Deforestation has substantiated the problem of climate change.
sentences.explanation:
"Substantiate" means to PROVE or SUPPORT with evidence — it doesn't mean to worsen or cause something.

✅ Correct: "Deforestation has exacerbated the problem of climate change."

This is a common Band 6 error — using sophisticated words without understanding their precise meaning.

sentences.text: She failed to substantiate her argument with concrete examples.

title: 🔑 Using These Words in IELTS Writing

sections.heading: In introductions
sections.body:
Avoid: "There are many problems with technology."
Better: "While technological advancements have proliferated across all sectors, they have simultaneously exacerbated pre-existing social inequalities."

sections.heading: In body paragraphs
sections.body:
Avoid: "The government should do something about pollution."
Better: "Governments must implement comprehensive strategies to mitigate the environmental impact of industrial expansion — a claim well-substantiated by recent climate research."

highlight: One sophisticated word used correctly is worth more than five simple words. Quality always beats quantity.

question: Which sentence demonstrates the BEST lexical resource for Band 8?
options: Technology is a very important thing in our lives nowadays.
The proliferation of digital devices has fundamentally transformed how we communicate.
There are more and more technologies that people use a lot.
Technology has become very, very common in modern daily life.
correct: The proliferation of digital devices has fundamentally transformed how we communicate.
explanation:
✅ "Proliferation" (sophisticated noun), "digital devices" (precise), "fundamentally transformed" (strong verb phrase), "communicate" (precise verb).

❌ The others use vague words: "important thing", "a lot", "very, very common" — all Band 5–6 language.

Band 8+ avoids vague intensifiers (very, really, a lot) and replaces them with precise vocabulary.
hint: Look for precise, specific language — not vague or repetitive words.
